headline: Krishival Foods Limited: Listing of Equity Shares pursuant to Rights Issue
sum: Krishival Foods Limited has completed listing of equity shares on NSE following a rights issue, marking capital-raising activity through proportional share issuance to existing shareholders.
implication: Rights issues in India trigger SEBI disclosure norms, preferential allotment rules, and listing compliance; this structure preserves shareholder preemption rights while enabling dilution-controlled capital access.
detail: Krishival Foods informed the NSE Exchange of the listing of equity shares issued pursuant to a rights offering. Rights issues in India are governed by the Companies Act, 2013 (Section 62) and SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018. The company must have obtained prior shareholder approval via special resolution, published an offer document, and complied with listing agreement norms. The August 18 listing date indicates successful closure and allotment of the rights issue.

framework.note: Central: Preferential allotment and rights issuance require special resolution of shareholders; sets the statutory gate for offer price and issue size.

framework.ref: SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018 – Part A (Preferential Allotment)
framework.note: Central: Prescribes valuation method, offer document, pricing, and disclosure of material information; rights issues must comply with minimum price norms.

framework.ref: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 – Regulation 30
framework.note: Central: Requires immediate disclosure of rights issue announcement, terms, allotment, and listing to the exchange.
Central: Governs the conduct of the listing, trading, and post-listing compliance obligations.
Applies to Board authority to approve the rights issue terms prior to shareholder resolution.
Applies to ensure no unpublished price-sensitive information is used by insiders during subscription period.
Applies to allottees; receipt of shares via rights issue may have tax implications (premium over face value).
